set.st: Indian story: at war, the Ottawas paddled across Little Traverse Bay, up the Bear River a short way and buried gold bars in strong boxes on the shore; all who knew the spot were killed. A local hermit dug there for years; the spot later became a gravel pit. Pin covers the river reach south of the city, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Bear River reach south of Petoskey (1913 gravel pit, not yet placed).
pinev: Reach-level: the 1913 account puts the pit in a farm gravel pit on the bank of Bear River south of Petoskey; the pin covers the river reach through secs 5, 8, 17 and 16 T34N R5W. The pit owner bought after 1902, so the 1902 plat cannot fix it (about 2.5 km).

set.pl: 20-acre farm, S part of W½ SE¼ sec. 27 T1N R6W (Bellevue Twp), about 1 mi east of Bellevue; Battle Creek River about ¼ mi north (1913 Eaton County atlas). The 1914 digging was 'back of the swamp' on this farm. The topo shows a marsh just N toward Battle Creek and a large wooded wetland about 250 m S on the neighbour's land.
